title: Sayf al-Muluk and Princess Badi'a al-Jamal

full_text:
Prince Sayf al-Muluk of Egypt inherited from his father an ancient, magical tunic embroidered with pearls, upon which was woven the portrait of Princess Badi'a al-Jamal, daughter of the King of the Jinns of the Mountain of Ruby. Struck by her radiant likeness, the prince vowed to search the world until he found her.

He built a fleet of forty ships and sailed into the uncharted eastern seas. For years he endured tempestuous shipwrecks, fought giant sea-monsters, escaped the Isle of Apes, and was saved by a friendly giant eagle that bore him across the clouds to the City of the Enchanters.

There he befriended an elderly, blind sage who instructed him in the magical counter-spells necessary to enter the subterranean palaces of the Jinns.

With unshakeable faith and pure courage, Sayf al-Muluk crossed the Sea of Glass, passed through the Valley of Rubies, and presented himself before the court of the King of the Jinns.

Princess Badi'a al-Jamal, who had dreamed of the Egyptian prince for years, recognized his noble heart and faithful devotion. The King of the Jinns, testing the prince with three riddles of astronomy and statecraft, found him wiser than his chief counselors.

The royal lovers were united in grand celebration, returning to Egypt to rule their realm in justice, demonstrating that true love guided by steadfast courage overcomes the barriers between mortal earth and the realms of enchantment.
moral: Faithful perseverance through perilous oceans and enchanted realms reaches its destined joy.
